title: Reconciliation
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Reconciliation means that God brings enemies into peace with Himself through Jesus Christ. Because of sin, people are alienated from God, but through Christ they are restored to relationship with Him.
summary: Reconciliation means that God brings enemies into peace with Himself through Jesus Christ. Because of sin, people are alienated from God, but through Christ they are restored to relationship with Him.
christFocus: Jesus Christ reconciles sinners to God by His death. Through Him, hostility is answered, peace is made, and those once far off are brought near to the Father.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Sin is not merely a personal struggle; it creates enmity with God. Sinners need more than forgiveness of guilt. They need to be brought back into peace with the God they have offended.

Reconciliation is God’s work in Christ. God does not wait for enemies to make themselves acceptable. He acts through the cross to bring sinners near.

Christ’s death is the ground of reconciliation. Through His body and blood, He makes peace and presents His people holy and blameless before God.

Those reconciled to God are entrusted with the message of reconciliation. The church announces that God is calling sinners to be reconciled to Him through Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people think their problem with God is distance, confusion, or disappointment only. Scripture says the deeper issue is enmity caused by sin. Reconciliation shows the seriousness of sin and the tenderness of God’s saving peace.

This doctrine also brings hope to the rejected and alienated. In Christ, those who were far off can be brought near—not merely tolerated, but welcomed into peace with God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive the peace God gives through Christ. Stop trying to negotiate your own terms with God. Come through the cross, where reconciliation has been made, and carry the message of reconciliation to others with humility and urgency.
